birth.traditional: Marga Sirsha Sudha Navami of Vibhava Nama Samvatsaram, in Revati Nakshatram and Kanya Lagnam — Thursday, 21 December 1928, at 00:45.

honours.text: Doctorate conferred by Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University.

sections.title: The teaching
body: Guruji taught Sanathana Dharma as something to be lived rather than merely believed, holding together its theory and its daily practice. He drew equally on the example of Lord Sri Rama and Lord Sri Krishna, and from that pairing comes the teaching at the centre of his work: God as Man, and Man as God.

He wrote and spoke for the householder rather than the renunciate — for people with work, families and obligations, who wanted to know what dharma asked of them in the circumstances they actually had.

sections.title: Anandavanam
body: After retiring from government service he built a small house in a mango grove at Bheemunipatnam and named it Anandavan. As people who followed his teaching came to live nearby, it became a settlement — though never an institution. Visitors to Anandavan are guests at Guruji's residence; there is no ashram there.

sections.title: Writing and public work
body: Guruji wrote more than five hundred articles on Indian culture, history and dharma for Andhra Bhumi, later collected as Bharateeyatha. He founded the cultural magazine Supatha in 1998, wrote a commentary on the Katha Upanishad, and produced work on the maharishis, on the history of Andhra, and on India's cultural links with South-East Asia.
His screen work includes Mana Katha, broadcast by Doordarshan as a thirteen-episode serial and awarded a state Nandi, and Tathagata Buddha, which received the Special Jury Nandi award.

sections.title: The trusts
body: Guruji established four trusts to carry the work forward: the Sanathana Dharma Charitable Trust, the Siva Ganga Sangeeta Parishad, the Mahalakshmi Temple Charitable Trust and the Sivanandaguru Cultural Trust, with centres at Bheemunipatnam and Warangal.

__note: Birth details, the 2005 doctorate and family names are verified from sdctbheemili.org. The narrative sections summarise material published across the Trust's own pages; the live biography page carries mainly photographs, so a fuller account should be supplied by the Trust.
